extracted.intended_audience: moviegoers, site visitors, and film reviewers (general audience and critics)
extracted.subtask_description: Rubrics and evaluative dimensions visible on a Rotten Tomatoes movie page: site-level metrics (Tomatometer, Popcornmeter), critics' consensus and reviews, audience reviews and moderation rules, plus the common critical dimensions called out in reviews (acting, directing, pacing, tone, production).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tomatometer
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Site-level aggregated critics metric shown prominently next to the title (percentage and number of critic reviews). Used as a quick indicator of critical approval on the film's page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Popcornmeter (audience rating)
rubrics_metrics.description: Popcornmeter — Fewer than 50 Ratings (audience metric displayed alongside Tomatometer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audience-sourced rating shown on the page; requires user participation to populate. Community Watch rules apply: users must write a review for their rating to count toward the Popcornmeter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community Watch moderation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: "Please write a review for your rating to count toward the Popcornmeter."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ratings are tied to written reviews and are subject to moderation: "Your review is awaiting approval. Once accepted, your review will get its big debut in the Popcornmeter. Visit FAQ to learn more about Community Watch." This implies ratings may be delayed/filtered and only count after approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critics Consensus
rubrics_metrics.description: Anchored by Stephan James' soulful performance and Rashad Frett's assured direction, Ricky is a raw, empathetic, and quietly powerful parable that delivers a moving gut punch through its realistic portrayal of life after incarceration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A short editorial summary synthesizing critics' common evaluative points; serves as a capsule judgment highlighting lead performance, direction, tone, emotional impact, and realism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual Critics' review scores and excerpts
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics' reviews with individual scores (examples shown: 3/4, 2.5/4, C) and short excerpts commenting on performance, directing, texture, pacing and thematic focus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critic entries provide granular judgements and evidence (e.g., "James gives a phenomenal performance that will shatter you," "A blunt film best when investing in day-to-day textures"). Different critics use different scoring scales (numeric fractions, star scales, letter grades); read excerpts for specific strengths/weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acting / Lead performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead acting highlighted as a key evaluative dimension: e.g., "Stephan James' soulful performance," "James gives a phenomenal performance," "Stephan James is intense as the lead Ricky."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics and audiences often judge a film by the lead's authenticity, intensity, and ability to carry emotional weight; supporting performances (e.g., Simbi Khali, Sheryl Lee Ralph, Titus Welliver) are also noted for adding depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direction / Directorial approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Direction called out (e.g., "Rashad Frett's assured direction," "Inobtrusive directing," "Director Rashad Frett won Best Director at Sundance").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators consider tone control, rhythm, and the director's handling of intimate vs intense scenes; comments mention effectiveness in maintaining rhythm that shifts between intense scenes and quiet moments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realism and portrayal of subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Realistic portrayal of life after incarceration is a repeated praise: "realistic portrayal of life after incarceration," "raw, empathetic."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics value authentic, empathetic depictions of real-world experiences and whether the film convincingly renders post-incarceration challenges and independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone balance and genre mixing
rubrics_metrics.description: Tone balance highlighted by audience/critic comments: "blending laughter, tears, and suspense," "balance between comedy, drama, and suspense, with well-timed humorous beats."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations address whether the film sustains an appropriate balance of emotional registers (humor, drama, suspense) and whether humorous beats relieve or undercut dramatic weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pacing and narrative resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Pacing and ending are noted as evaluative points: "The last 15 minutes of the gritty drama Ricky are a little too rushed and oversimplified."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics judge whether the film's ending and pacing resolve themes satisfactorily and whether late-act changes feel rushed or earned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production elements (cinematography, sound design, key scenes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Production values are highlighted in audience review: "The direction is effective, maintaining a rhythm... the production—cinematography, sound design, and key scenes—intensifies the emotions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical craft (camera work, sound, scene construction) is used as evidence for emotional impact and storytelling effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional impact / thematic potency
rubrics_metrics.description: Emotional effect is emphasized across consensus and audience reviews: phrases like "moving gut punch," "makes you really feel," "gripping story," "gut-wrenching performances."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess how powerfully a film moves viewers, how it makes them empathize with characters, and whether it provokes thought or emotional response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting cast and character depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Supporting performances and character roles are singled out: "supporting characters add depth and relief," "Simbi Khali as Ricky's mother almost steals the show."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations consider the contributions of supporting actors to narrative richness and emotional nuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synopsis / Movie metadata as decision factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Movie Info fields (Synopsis, Director, Producers, Screenwriters, Distributor, Production Companies, Genre, Language, Release Date, Runtime) are provided on the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These metadata fields are used by audiences to decide interest and contextualize reviews (genre expectations, runtime, release format). While not evaluative rules per se, they function as criteria for viewing choices.
